items.question: In what manner must instruction be delivered after separate division?
premises: Instruction involves a prior act of division.
The divided elements are treated separately.
Teaching is explicitly given after this separation.
items.inference: Proper instruction requires dividing the subject and teaching each part distinctly.
uncertainties: The repeated upadiṣṭam may be emphatic or a textual duplication.
items.plain_english: Having divided it separately, it has been taught, taught.

items.question: According to whose intention should the application of these teachings proceed?
premises: The application concerns these previously mentioned elements.
An intention or purpose governs the application.
The manner of being should conform to that intention.
items.inference: The teaching should be applied in accordance with the intended purpose.
uncertainties: Whether abhiprāya restates or specifies yathābhiprāyam is unclear.
items.plain_english: It should be according to the intention of these; that is the intention.

items.question: What verbal act must accompany the reception of the teaching?
premises: The recipient is commanded to receive.
A concluding utterance is marked by thus.
One should inform or present accordingly.
items.inference: Reception of the teaching must be accompanied by a formal act of informing.
uncertainties: The repeated nivedayet may be emphatic or a textual duplication.
items.plain_english: Receive it, thus one should inform, should inform.

items.question: By what paths can the intended meaning be obtained?
premises: There are blossomed middle paths.
These paths function as means.
The meaning is obtainable through them.
items.inference: The intended meaning is attained through the blossomed middle paths.
uncertainties: The exact referent of vikasita-madhyama-mārgaiḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: The meaning is obtainable through the blossomed middle paths.

items.question: What condition of pervasion holds in that stated context?
premises: A state is said to come about.
That state is located in a specific context.
Pervasion exists there.
items.inference: In that context, pervasion is present as the resulting condition.
uncertainties: The scope of tatra is not fully specified in this unit.
items.plain_english: Thus it becomes; there, pervasion exists.

items.question: Which practitioners are qualified to perform the prescribed worship?
premises: Worship is the act in question.
Adepts are involved in the practice.
The best householders are specified as agents.
items.inference: The prescribed worship is performed by the best householders who are adepts.
uncertainties: The compound relation between sādhaka and uttamaiḥ gṛhasthaiḥ is interpretive.
items.plain_english: Worship is by the best householder adepts.

items.question: What kind of worship should be commenced according to this instruction?
premises: Worship is the object to be undertaken.
There is an injunction to begin it.
The worship is characterized as external.
items.inference: One should begin external worship as the intended practice.
uncertainties: arthaḥ may function as a glossing marker rather than part of the injunction.
items.plain_english: One should begin external worship; that is the meaning.

items.question: What constitutes the worship indicated in this ritual context?
premises: Worship is described as being performed.
A group of mantras is involved in the sacrifice.
By this alone the worship here is indicated.
items.inference: The indicated worship here consists in worship through that mantra-group alone.
uncertainties: The precise antecedent of anenaiva is not explicit in this unit.
items.plain_english: It is worshipped, thus: by this mantra-group of the sacrifice alone, worship is indicated here.

items.question: At what stages must the placement of power be remembered?
premises: This placement of power is under discussion.
It was relevant previously.
It must be remembered even at the beginning of internal worship.
items.inference: The placement of power must be remembered both previously and at the start of internal worship.
uncertainties: The exact scope of pūrvatra relative to antaryāga is compressed.
items.plain_english: And this placement of power, previously and even at the beginning of internal worship, must be remembered.

items.question: How is the continuation of the preceding sequence formally marked?
premises: A continuation marker is used.
The marker is repeated.
The sequence is closed with a concluding marker.
items.inference: The text signals an open-ended continuation of the preceding sequence.
uncertainties: The specific items included in the continuation are not stated.
items.plain_english: And so forth, and so forth, thus beginning.

items.question: What result follows for the adept when the prescribed act is completed?
premises: A prescribed act is completed.
The adept is the subject affected.
The adept becomes a vessel for supreme success.
items.inference: Upon completion of the act, the adept becomes fit for supreme attainment.
uncertainties: The specific act referred to by kṛte sati depends on prior context.
items.plain_english: When this is done, the adept becomes a vessel for supreme success; that is the meaning.

items.question: By what alternative means may the spoken worship be performed?
premises: A form of worship has been spoken.
Alternative means are presented.
Worship may be performed even by mind alone.
items.inference: The spoken worship may be performed by śāmbūka and others or even mentally alone.
uncertainties: The identity and role of śāmbūka in this context is unclear.
items.plain_english: As spoken, one should worship even by śāmbūka and others, or indeed by mind alone; that is the meaning.
